paragraphs: Ramaco Resources, Inc. (the "Company," "Ramaco," "we," "us," or "our") is a Delaware corporation formed in October 2016. Our principal corporate and executive offices are located in Lexington, Kentucky with operational offices in Charleston, West Virginia and Sheridan, Wyoming. We are a dual platform critical mineral company that is both an operator and developer of high-quality, low-cost metallurgical coal in southern West Virginia and southwestern Virginia, and a developing producer of coal, rare earth elements and critical minerals in Wyoming. Our metallurgical coal development portfolio primarily includes the following properties: Elk Creek, Berwind, Knox Creek, and Maben. We believe each of these properties possesses geologic and logistical advantages that make our coal among the lowest delivered-cost U.S. metallurgical coal to our domestic customer base, North American blast furnace steel mills and coke plants, as well as to international metallurgical coal consumers. In mid-2025, we initiated development of our rare earth element and critical mineral operations near Sheridan, Wyoming (the "Brook Mine"). The Brook Mine initially produced

representative ore material to serve as feedstock for testing, with the goal of demonstrating the viability of processing rare earth elements and critical minerals at a full-scale commercial facility and ultimately establishing mineral reserves and resources. Contiguous to the Brook Mine, the Company operates a carbon research facility related to the production of advanced carbon products and materials from coal. The Company's operations are organized into two reportable segments: Metallurgical Coal and Rare Earths and Critical Minerals. See Note 14--Segment Reporting in Item 8, Part II for additional information.

We are an operator and developer of high-quality, low-cost metallurgical coal in southern West Virginia and southwestern Virginia. We maintain 85 million reserve tons and 1,337 million measured and indicated resource tons of high-quality metallurgical coal. We believe our advantaged reserve geology provides us with higher productivity and industry-leading lower cash costs.

As of December 31, 2025, our operations included six active mines at our Elk Creek mining complex (the "Elk Creek Complex"), one active mine at our Berwind mining complex (the "Berwind Complex"), one active mine at our Knox Creek mining complex (the "Knox Creek Complex"), and one active mine at our Maben mining complex (the "Maben Complex"). We maintained four additional mines in idle status across our portfolio of mining complexes that can be reactivated when market conditions warrant.

Development of the Elk Creek Complex commenced in 2016 and included the construction of a preparation plant and rail load-out facilities. The Elk Creek property consists of approximately 20,200 acres of controlled mineral rights and contains approximately 16 seams targeted for production. The Elk Creek Complex produces high-volatile A and B metallurgical coals. Expansion of the Elk Creek preparation plant occurred in 2022 and 2023 in order to increase production, and high-volatile additions at the Elk Creek Complex occurred during 2024, which were fully in production by the end of the third quarter of 2024.

Development of the Berwind Complex began in late 2017. In 2020, we suspended development at the Berwind Complex due to lower pricing and demand largely caused by the COVID-19 outbreak. In early 2021, as pricing and demand improved, Berwind development was restarted. We successfully reached the thicker Pocahontas No. 4 seam in late 2021. The Berwind property consists of approximately 62,500 acres of controlled mineral rights, including the December 2021 acquisition of "Amonate Assets" from subsidiaries of Coronado Global Resources Inc. ("Coronado") in 2021. The Amonate Assets include a processing plant located in our Berwind Complex, saving us transportation costs to our Knox Creek plant, 26 miles away. The Berwind Complex experienced an ignition event in 2022 that resulted in idling mining operations for one of the active mines. Production restarted for the idle mine in the first quarter of 2023. The Berwind Complex currently produces low-volatile and mid-volatile metallurgical coal. The Company continues to increase production at the main Berwind low-volatile mine.

Our Knox Creek Complex includes a preparation plant and 88,850 acres of controlled mineral rights. The Complex currently produces mid and high-volatile metallurgical coal and also processes and ships coal from other third-party operators. The Company closed its Jawbone mine during 2024, which was nearing the end of its mine life and experiencing higher costs of production. In November 2025, the Company acquired what it refers to as the Russell County property which are contiguous with the Knox Creek complex and which is expected to significantly increase the reserves and resources at Knox Creek.

The Maben Coal acquisition in 2022 provides the Company with 28,000 leased acres of controlled mineral rights, which includes coal deposits that may be mined currently by surface and highwall mining methods as well as developed in the future through deep mining. The Maben Complex currently produces low-volatile metallurgical coal. The Company commissioned a preparation plant at the Maben Complex during 2024 in order to reduce trucking costs.

Our RAM Mine property is located in southwestern Pennsylvania. Following years of delays, the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection issued a denial of the RAM Mine permit during 2023. While the Company believes that the RAM permit was denied incorrectly and capriciously, we will not appeal the denial of the permit and will instead focus on our other core properties and monetize these assets at the appropriate time.

As of December 31, 2025, our estimated aggregate annual production capacity is approximately four million clean tons of coal, excluding our idled properties. We plan to complete development of our existing properties and increase annual production over the next few years to possibly more than seven million clean tons of metallurgical coal annually, subject to market conditions, permitting, and additional capital deployment in the medium-term. We may also acquire additional reserves or infrastructure that contribute to our focus on advantaged geology and lower costs.

Our Brook Mine property consists of approximately 15,800 acres of controlled mineral rights and a research and development facility that were acquired as part of the purchase of Ramaco Coal in 2022. The mine is currently undergoing rigorous third-party testing and analysis to assess the potential for commercial development of rare earth elements and critical minerals. In July 2025, the Fluor Corporation ("Fluor") issued a Preliminary Economic Assessment (the "PEA") in which it concluded that the Brook Mine was both technically and economically viable based on its findings and the product pricing information provided by the Company.

Metallurgical coal, also known as "met coal" or "coking coal," is a key component of the blast furnace steelmaking process and, therefore, demand for such coal is highly correlated with conditions in the steel industry. The global metallurgical coal market has grown steadily in recent years and will likely continue to grow over the next few years driven by the industrialization of emerging economies and expansion of urbanization globally.

United States metallurgical coal mines are primarily located in the Appalachian area of the eastern U.S. Imported metallurgical coal has historically been uneconomic due to transportation costs and availability of domestic supply. Metallurgical coal is transported to domestic customers by truck, rail, barge and vessel. Metallurgical coal contracts in North America are typically 12-month, calendar year contracts where both prices and volumes are fixed. These contracts are normally negotiated and entered into during the third and fourth quarters of the preceding calendar year.

U.S. metallurgical coal is also exported to the seaborne market and sold to buyers in Europe, South America, Africa, and Asia. U.S. metallurgical coal exports are sold to buyers in the Atlantic Basin market (customers in Europe, Brazil and Africa) as well as buyers in the Pacific Basin (customers in India, South Korea, Japan and China). U.S. metallurgical coal exports compete with Australian metallurgical coals that are generally produced at a lower cost but are geographically disadvantaged to the Atlantic Basin. Conversely, Australian production has a much shorter logistical route to Pacific Basin customers. Any supply shortfall out of Australia, or increase in global demand beyond Australia's capacity, has historically been serviced by U.S. and Canadian metallurgical coal producers.

We do not currently have rare earth elements or critical mineral reserves, and our growth prospects may be adversely affected if we are unable to successfully develop the Brook Mine into a commercial scale mine.
Consolidation of the rare earth elements and critical minerals industry may result in increased competition.

We have customer concentration, so the loss of, or significant reduction in, purchases by our largest coal customers could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
Our customer base is highly dependent on the steel industry.
We do not enter into long-term sales contracts for our coal, and as a result, we are exposed to fluctuations in market pricing.
The failure to access coal preparation facilities may have a material adverse effect on our ability to produce coal for our prospective customers and to meet quality specifications.
Product alternatives or other technologies may reduce demand for our products.

We face uncertainties in estimating our economically recoverable coal reserves, and inaccuracies in our estimates could result in lower-than-expected revenues, higher than expected costs and decreased profitability.
Our inability to acquire additional coal reserves that are economically recoverable may have a material adverse effect on our future profitability.
We are dependent on contractors for the successful completion of the development of our properties.

The availability and reliability of transportation facilities and fluctuations in transportation costs could affect the demand for our coal or impair our ability to supply coal to prospective customers.
If customers do not enter into, extend or honor contracts with us, our profitability could be adversely affected.
paragraphs: Our business involves certain risks and uncertainties. The following is a description of significant risks that might cause our future financial condition or results of operations to differ materially from those expected. In addition to the risks and uncertainties described below, we may face other risks and uncertainties, some of which may be unknown to us and some of which we may deem immaterial. If one or more of these risks or uncertainties occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations may be materially and adversely affected. A summary of our risk factors is as follows:
Our growth prospects may be adversely affected by fluctuations in demand for, and prices of, rare earth elements and critical minerals.

We do not currently have rare earth elements or critical mineral reserves, and our growth prospects may be adversely affected if we are unable to successfully develop the Brook Mine into a commercial scale mine.

An increase in the global supply of rare earth element products, dumping, predatory pricing and other anti-competitive tactics taken by our competitors may materially and adversely affect our growth prospects and the price of our common stock.
Consolidation of the rare earth elements and critical minerals industry may result in increased competition.

Certain of our properties have not yet been fully developed into producing coal mines and, if we experience any development delays or cost increases or are unable to complete the construction of our facilities, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.

paragraphs: The following discussion is intended to assist you in understanding our results of operations and our present financial condition and contains forward-looking statements that reflect our future plans, estimates, beliefs and expected performance. The forward-looking statements are dependent upon events, risks and uncertainties that may be outside our control. We caution you that our actual results could differ materially from those discussed in these forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause or contribute to such differences are discussed elsewhere in this Annual Report, particularly in the "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors," all of which are difficult to predict. In light of these risks, uncertainties and assumptions, the forward-looking events discussed may not occur. We do not undertake any obligation to publicly update any forward-looking statements except as otherwise required by applicable law.

We are a dual platform critical mineral company that is both an operator and developer of high-quality, low-cost metallurgical coal in southern West Virginia and southwestern Virginia, and a developing producer of coal, rare earth and critical minerals in Wyoming. Our metallurgical coal development portfolio primarily includes the following properties: Elk Creek, Berwind, Knox Creek, and Maben. We believe each of these properties possesses geologic and logistical advantages that make our coal among the lowest delivered-cost U.S. metallurgical coal to our domestic customer base, North American blast furnace steel mills and coke plants, as well as to international metallurgical coal consumers. In mid-2025, we initiated development of our rare earth element and critical mineral operations near Sheridan, Wyoming (the "Brook Mine"). The Brook Mine initially produced representative ore material to serve as feedstock for testing, with the goal of demonstrating the viability of processing rare earth elements and critical minerals at a full-scale commercial facility and ultimately establishing mineral reserves and resources. Contiguous to the Brook Mine, the Company operates a carbon research facility related to the production of advanced carbon products and materials from coal.

Our reportable segments, which are primarily based on the Company's internal organizational structure and types of controlled mineral deposits, are its two operating segments—Metallurgical Coal and Rare Earths and Critical Minerals. Where applicable, prior period amounts have been recast to conform to this segment reporting structure, which was modified during the third quarter of 2025.

Our primary source of revenue is the sale of metallurgical coal. We maintain 85 million reserve tons and 1,337 million measured and indicated resource tons of high-quality metallurgical coal. Our plan is to continue the development of our existing properties and grow annual production over the next few years to possibly as much as seven million clean tons of metallurgical coal annually, subject to market conditions, permitting and additional capital deployment in the medium-term. We may also acquire additional reserves or infrastructure that contribute to our focus on advantaged geology and lower costs.

The overall outlook of the metallurgical coal business is dependent on a variety of factors such as pricing, regulatory uncertainties, and global economic conditions. Coal consumption and production in the U.S. are driven by several market dynamics and trends including the U.S. and global economies, the U.S. dollar's strength relative to other currencies and accelerating production cuts. Blast furnace steelmaking is more prevalent outside the U.S. compared to domestic steel production, which creates demand for exports of metallurgical coal, including demand growth in Asia Pacific.

Global metallurgical coal markets softened in 2024 and continued to do so in 2025 due to constrained economic growth in some regions of the world and continued conflict overseas. The global steel market experienced slower growth, especially in China, resulting in elevated levels of Chinese steel exports. These conditions have led steel companies to both cut back on their own production and to reduce the price they are willing to pay for their metallurgical coal feedstock. Overall steel demand will likely remain weak in the near term; however, supply cuts may occur for higher cost operations absent a significant upward movement in pricing. Longer term, the Company believes that limited global investment in new coking coal production capacity, the industrialization of emerging economies, expansion of urbanization globally, and an eventual return to economic growth will support coking coal markets overall.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we sold 3.8 million tons of coal and recognized $536.6 million of revenue. Of this amount, 37% of our revenue was from sales into North American markets, including Canada, and 63% of our revenue was from sales into export markets. During the same period of 2024, we sold 4.0 million tons of coal and recognized $666.3 million of revenue, of which 33% was from sales into North American markets, including Canada, and 67% was from sales into export markets. Sales into export markets, which often include index-based pricing, generally have greater exposure to variability in pricing from period to period. The Company's exports have not been materially delayed or otherwise affected by recent severe weather events, dockworker labor disputes, or recently enacted U.S. tariffs.

As of December 31, 2025, the Company had outstanding performance obligations of 1.1 million tons for contracts with fixed sales prices averaging $142 per ton, excluding freight, as well as 1.2 million tons for contracts with index-based pricing mechanisms. The Company expects to satisfy approximately 97% of the committed tons in 2026 and the remainder in 2027. Refer to Note 10—Revenues in Item 8, Part II for additional information.

The metallurgical coal markets are volatile in nature; therefore, the Company prioritizes managing its financial position and liquidity, while managing costs and capital expenditures and returning value to its shareholders.

In 2025, our segment capital expenditures were $60.5 million, excluding capitalized interest of $1.2 million. In 2024, our capital expenditures were $69.7 million, excluding capitalized interest of $1.5 million. The decrease in capital expenditures was due to lower spending in 2025 on the Company's strategic growth projects, specifically at the Maben preparation plant.
The Company produced 3.8 million tons in 2025 compared to 3.7 million tons in 2024 as a result of the increase in capacity and completed development work.

Our ongoing business development efforts are focused on the timely and prudent advancement of our rare earth elements and critical minerals operations, the establishment of associated processing facilities and the production of rare earth element minerals and coal-to-carbon based products and critical minerals products.

We plan to target the processing and production of a number of rare earth elements and critical minerals which include heavy magnetic rare earth elements, like terbium and dysprosium, and critical minerals, like gallium, germanium and scandium which are, from time to time subject to strict export licensing requirements and changing destination-specific restrictions (including export bans or restrictions to the United States) imposed by the Chinese government. These planned initiatives provide substantial growth opportunities in future periods.

In 2023, we announced the discovery of a major deposit of primary magnetic rare earth elements and critical minerals at our mine, the Brook Mine near Sheridan, Wyoming. The Brook Mine rare earth elements and critical minerals site has what we believe to be the largest unconventional deposit of rare earth elements and critical minerals discovered to date in the United States, as well as the first new rare earth elements mine in the United States in 70 years. We had a ribbon cutting and groundbreaking at the Brook Mine in July 2025 and the overall development of this mine and processing project is proceeding.

paragraphs: Ramaco Resources, Inc. (the "Company," "Ramaco," "we," "us," or "our") 是一家於2016年10月成立的特拉華州公司。本公司主要營業及行政辦公室位於肯塔基州列剋星敦，營運辦公室則位於西維吉尼亞州查爾斯敦與懷俄明州雪倫堡。本公司為一家雙平台關鍵礦物公司，同時為南部西維吉尼亞州與西南維吉尼亞州高品質、低成本冶金煤的經營者與開發者，並為懷俄明州煤炭、稀土元素與關鍵礦物的開發生產者。本公司冶金煤開發資產主要包括以下礦區：Elk Creek、Berwind、Knox Creek 與 Maben。本公司相信這些礦區均具備地質與物流優勢，使本公司煤炭成為美國交付成本最低的冶金煤之一，服務於國內客戶羣體，即北美高爐鋼廠與焦炭廠，以及國際冶金煤消費者。2025年中旬，本公司開始在懷俄明州雪倫堡附近開發稀土元素與關鍵礦物業務（"Brook Mine"）。Brook Mine 首階段生產代表性的礦石材料，作為測試用原料，目標為展示在全規模商業設施中處理稀土元素與關鍵礦物的可行性，並最終建立礦物儲備與資源。Brook Mine 鄰近處，本公司運營與生產先進碳產品與材料相關的碳研究設施。本公司業務分為兩個應報告分部：冶金煤與稀土元素與關鍵礦物。有關更多資訊，請參閱第14項註釋--分部報告，位於第8項，第二部分。
本公司為南部西維吉尼亞州與西南維吉尼亞州高品質、低成本冶金煤的經營者與開發者。本公司擁有85百萬噸的儲備煤與1,337百萬噸的測量與指示資源煤。本公司相信本公司具備優勢儲備地質，使本公司擁有更高的生產力與行業領先的低成本現金開支。
本公司為南部西維吉尼亞州及西南部維吉尼亞州高品質、低成本冶金煤的運營商與開發商。本公司持有85百萬噸儲備煤及1,337百萬噸測量與指示資源煤。本公司認為，我們具優勢的儲備地質條件使我們擁有更高的生產力及業界領先的較低現金成本。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司業務包含位於Elk Creek礦區複合體（"Elk Creek Complex"）的六座活躍礦區，位於Berwind礦區複合體（"Berwind Complex"）的一座活躍礦區，位於Knox Creek礦區複合體（"Knox Creek Complex"）的一座活躍礦區，以及位於Maben礦區複合體（"Maben Complex"）的一座活躍礦區。本公司在礦區複合體中維持四座額外的閒置礦區，當市場條件允許時可重新啟動。

Elk Creek Complex 的開發於 2016 年展開，包含建設準備廠與鐵路裝載設施。Elk Creek 資源區約有 20,200 英畝的控制礦權，並包含約 16 層煤層可供生產。Elk Creek Complex 生產高揮發性 A 與 B 金屬用煤。Elk Creek 備料廠的擴建於 2022 年與 2023 年進行，以增加生產量，且 Elk Creek Complex 的高揮發性煤層增產於 2024 年進行，並於 2024 年第三季末完全投入生產。

Berwind Complex 的開發於 2017 年晚些時候展開。2020 年，因價格下跌與需求減少，主要由於 COVID-19 疫情爆發，我們暫停了 Berwind Complex 的開發。2021 年初，隨著價格與需求改善，Berwind 的開發重新啟動。我們於 2021 年底成功鑽入較厚的 Pocahontas No. 4 煤層。Berwind 資源區約有 62,500 英畝的控制礦權，包含 2021 年 12 月從 Coronado Global Resources Inc.（"Coronado"）子公司取得的 "Amonate Assets"。Amonate Assets 包含位於 Berwind Complex 的處理廠，節省我們至 Knox Creek 廠區 26 英里遠的運輸成本。2022 年，Berwind Complex 發生火災事件，導致其中一個運作中的礦坑暫停生產。該暫停礦坑於 2023 年第一季恢復生產。Berwind Complex 目前生產低揮發性與中揮發性金屬用煤。本公司持續增加主要 Berwind 低揮發性礦坑的生產量。

Knox Creek Complex 包含準備廠與 88,850 英畝的控制礦權。該 Complex 目前生產中揮發性與高揮發性金屬用煤，並處理與運輸其他第三方經營者的煤。本公司於 2024 年關閉 Jawbone 礦，該礦接近礦場壽命末期且生產成本較高。2025 年 11 月，本公司取得其所稱的 Russell County 資源區，該資源區與 Knox Creek Complex 相鄰，預期將顯著增加 Knox Creek 的儲備與資源。
2022 年取得 Maben Coal 的交易，使本公司取得 28,000 英畝的控制礦權，包含可透過露天與高壁開採方式目前開採，以及未來透過深層開採開發的煤層。Maben Complex 目前生產低揮發性金屬用煤。本公司於 2024 年在 Maben Complex 委託建設準備廠，以降低運輸成本。
本公司之 RAM Mine 資源位於美國賓夕法尼亞州西南部。經過多年的延宕後，賓夕法尼亞州環境保護部於 2023 年發出 RAM Mine 許可證的否決通知。雖然本公司認為 RAM 許可證被否決是錯誤且隨意的，但本公司將不會對此許可證的否決提出上訴，並轉而專注於其他核心資源，並在適當的時間 monetize 這些資產。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司預估的年度總生產能力約為四百萬潔淨噸煤，不包含已停產的資源。本公司計畫完成現有資源的開發，並在未來幾年內提高年度生產量，可能達到超過七百萬潔淨噸冶金煤的年生產量，但需視市場條件、許可證及中短期額外資金投入而定。本公司也可能取得額外的儲備或基礎設施，以強化本公司在優勢地質與較低成本的重點。

本公司之 Brook Mine 資源包含約 15,800 英畝的控制礦權及一個研究與開發設施，這些資源係於 2022 年購買 Ramaco Coal 時取得。該礦目前正進行嚴謹的第三方測試與分析，以評估開發稀土元素與關鍵礦物的商業潛力。2025 年 7 月，Fluor Corporation（"Fluor"）發佈了一份初步經濟評估（"PEA"），其中結論指出，根據其研究結果及本公司提供的產品價格資訊，Brook Mine 在技術與經濟上皆具可行性。
冶金煤，亦稱為 "met coal" 或 "coking coal"，是高爐煉鋼過程中的關鍵零組件，因此對此類煤的需求與鋼鐵產業的狀況高度相關。全球冶金煤市場近年來穩定成長，未來幾年可能持續成長，主要由新興經濟體的工業化及全球城市化的擴張所驅動。
美國的冶金煤礦主要位於美國東部的阿巴拉契亞地區。進口的冶金煤過去因運輸成本及國內供應充足，一直不具經濟效益。冶金煤透過卡車、鐵路、船隻及船舶運輸至國內客戶。北美地區的冶金煤合約通常為 12 個月的曆年合約，其中價格與數量皆為固定。這些合約通常於前一年的第三及第四季進行談判與簽訂。

美國的冶金煤亦出口至海運市場，並銷售給歐洲、南美洲、非洲及亞洲的買家。美國的冶金煤出口銷售給位於大西洋盆地市場（歐洲、巴西及非洲的客戶）以及太平洋盆地市場（印度、南韓、日本及中國的客戶）的買家。美國的冶金煤出口與澳洲的冶金煤競爭，澳洲的冶金煤通常生產成本較低，但地理上對大西洋盆地不利。相反，澳洲的生產至太平洋盆地客戶的物流路線較短。若澳洲出現供應不足，或全球需求超過澳洲的生產能力，歷史經驗顯示將由美國及加拿大冶金煤生產者來補足。

paragraphs: 以下討論旨在協助您瞭解我們的營運成果與目前財務狀況，並包含未來展望的陳述，反映我們未來的計畫、預估、信念與預期表現。未來展望的陳述取決於事件、風險與不確定性，這些可能在我們的控制範圍之外。我們提醒您，實際結果可能與這些未來展望的陳述有重大差異。造成或促成此差異的因素，已於本年度報告中其他部分討論，特別是在「未來展望陳述的警示」與「風險因素」，所有這些因素都難以預測。考慮到這些風險、不確定性與假設，所討論的未來事件可能不會發生。我們不承擔任何義務公開更新任何未來展望的陳述，除非法律另有規定。

本公司為雙平台關鍵礦物公司，同時為南部西維吉尼亞州與西南維吉尼亞州高品質、低成本冶金煤的運營者與開發者，並為懷俄明州煤炭、稀土與關鍵礦物的開發生產者。我們的冶金煤開發資產組主要包括以下礦區：Elk Creek、Berwind、Knox Creek 與 Maben。我們認為這些礦區均具備地質與物流優勢，使我們的煤炭成為美國交付成本最低的冶金煤之一，供應給國內客戶羣、北美高爐鋼鐵廠與焦炭廠，以及國際冶金煤消費者。2025 年中，我們開始在懷俄明州雪倫敦附近開發稀土元素與關鍵礦物業務（稱為「Brook Mine」）。Brook Mine 首先生產代表性的礦石材料，作為測試的原料，目標為展示在全規模商業設施中處理稀土元素與關鍵礦物的可行性，並最終建立礦物儲備與資源。與 Brook Mine 相鄰，本公司運營一個碳研究設施，與從煤炭生產先進碳產品與材料有關。
我們的應報告分部，主要根據本公司內部組織結構與控制的礦物儲備類型，為其兩個營運分部—冶金煤與稀土與關鍵礦物。在適用的情況下，先前期間的金額已重新整理以符合此分部報告結構，此結構於 2025 年第三季進行了修改。
本公司主要收入來源為冶金煤的銷售。本公司持有 85 百萬噸儲備量及 1,337 百萬噸測量及指標資源量的高品質冶金煤。本公司計畫持續發展現有資產，並在未來幾年內增加年產量，目標可能達到每年七百萬噸淨冶金煤，但需視市場情況、許可證及中長期追加資本部署而定。本公司亦可能取得額外儲備或基礎建設，以強化本公司在優勢地質及降低成本的重點。
冶金煤業務的整體展望取決於多種因素，例如價格、法規不確定性與全球經濟條件。美國的煤炭消費與生產受到多種市場動態與趨勢驅動，包括美國與全球經濟、美元相對於其他貨幣的強度以及加速的生產減產。高爐鋼鐵製造在美國以外地區比美國本土鋼鐵生產更為普遍，這創造了對冶金煤出口的需求，包括亞太地區的需求增長。

全球冶金煤市場在 2024 年趨於疲軟，並在 2025 年持續如此，這是因為世界某些地區經濟成長受到限制，以及海外衝突持續。全球鋼鐵市場成長較慢，特別是在中國，導致中國鋼鐵出口量增加。這些情況使鋼鐵公司同時減少自身的生產，並降低願意為冶金煤原料支付的價格。近期內，整體鋼鐵需求可能仍偏弱；然而，若價格沒有顯著上漲，高成本運營可能會出現供應減產。長期而言，本公司認為，全球對新焦煤生產能力投資有限、新興經濟體的工業化、全球城市化的擴張，以及經濟成長的最終回復，將支持焦煤市場整體。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司尚有未履行之績效義務，計1.1百萬公噸，為固定銷售價格之合約，平均每公噸142美元，不含運費，以及1.2百萬公噸，為基於指數價格機制之合約。本公司預期於2026年履行約97%之承諾公噸，餘者於2027年履行。有關更多資訊，請參閱第8項，第二部分，附註10—收入。
冶金煤市場本質上屬於波動性市場；因此，本公司優先管理其財務狀況與流動性，同時管理成本與資本支出，並回饋價值給股東。
2025 年，我們的應報告分部資本支出為 60.5 百萬美元，扣除資本化利息 1.2 百萬美元。2024 年，我們的資本支出為 69.7 百萬美元，扣除資本化利息 1.5 百萬美元。資本支出減少係因 2025 年本公司在戰略成長計畫上的支出較低，特別是在 Maben 製備廠的支出較少。
本公司於 2025 年生產 3.8 百萬公噸，較 2024 年的 3.7 百萬公噸增加，這是因應產能提升及已完成的開發工作所致。
我們持續的業務發展努力，聚焦於稀有金屬與關鍵礦物業務的及時且謹慎推進，建立相關加工設施，以及生產稀有金屬元素礦物與煤基碳產品與關鍵礦物產品。
我們計畫針對若干稀有金屬元素與關鍵礦物進行加工與生產，包括重磁性稀有金屬元素，如釤與鑭，以及關鍵礦物，如鋁、 germanium 與 scandium，這些礦物有時會受到中國政府所施加的嚴格出口許可要求與變動的目標地特定限制（包括對美國的出口禁令或限制）。這些計畫性質的措施為未來期間帶來顯著的成長機會。

2023 年，我們宣佈在 Sheridan，Wyoming 頑近的 Brook 礦發現一個主要的原生磁性稀有金屬元素與關鍵礦物儲量。Brook 礦的稀有金屬元素與關鍵礦物地點，據我們所知，是迄今為止美國發現的最大非傳統儲量的稀有金屬元素與關鍵礦物，同時也是美國 70 年來第一座新的稀有金屬元素礦。我們於 2025 年 7 月在 Brook 礦舉行開工典禮與動土儀式，該礦與加工專案的整體開發工作正在進行中。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的成長前景可能因稀有金屬與關鍵礦物的需求與價格波動而受到不利影響。
我們目前並未擁有稀有金屬與關鍵礦物的儲備，若我們無法成功將布魯克礦場開發為商業規模礦場，將可能對我們的成長前景造成不利影響。
稀有金屬與關鍵礦物產業的集中化可能導致競爭增加。
我們的客戶集中度較高，若我們最大的燃煤客戶減少或停止採購，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流造成不利影響。
我們的客戶羣高度依賴鋼鐵產業。
我們並未與客戶簽訂長期銷售合約，因此我們面臨市場價格波動的風險。
無法取得燃煤處理設施可能對我們生產符合品質規格的燃煤以服務潛在客戶的能力造成重大不利影響。
產品替代方案或其他技術可能降低我們產品的需求。
我們在估算經濟可採用煤儲量時面臨不確定性，且估算不準確可能導致收入低於預期、成本高於預期以及利潤率下降。
我們若無法取得經濟可採用的額外煤儲量，可能對我們未來的利潤率產生重大不利影響。
我們依賴承包商成功完成我們資產的開發。
運輸設施的可得性與可靠性以及運輸成本的波動可能影響我們煤的需求，或影響我們向潛在客戶供應煤的能力。
若客戶未與我們簽訂、延長或履行契約，可能對我們的利潤率產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 本公司業務涉及某些風險與不確定性。以下為可能導致本公司未來財務狀況或營運結果與預期有重大差異的重要風險說明。除下列所列風險與不確定性外，本公司亦可能面臨其他風險與不確定性，其中一些可能是本公司尚未知悉，一些本公司可能認為不重要。若其中一個或多個風險或不確定性發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。本公司風險因素之摘要如下：
本公司成長前景可能因稀土元素與關鍵礦物之需求與價格波動而受到不利影響。
本公司目前並未擁有稀土元素或關鍵礦物之儲備，若本公司無法成功將布魯克礦開發為商業規模礦場，將可能對本公司成長前景造成不利影響。
全球稀土元素產品供應增加、競爭對手採取傾銷、掠奪性 pricing 及其他不競爭行為，可能對本公司成長前景及本公司普通股之價格造成重大且不利影響。
稀土元素與關鍵礦物產業之集中化可能導致競爭增加。
本公司部分財產尚未完全開發為生產煤礦，若本公司遭遇任何開發延誤或成本增加，或無法完成設施建設，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
